title: How Slim and Slam got their name, with Martin Block
summary: After the WNEW broadcast, manager Martin Block backed them as an act; they searched for a name and settled on Slim and Slam in late 1935.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Now, you, when did you get the name, when did you get the nickname, Slam?

Well, that, after this program that I went down the next day and joined him on, we played a few numbers. And during, at that time the manager of the radio station, WNEW, was, his name was Martin[Block] And come to think of it, Martin Block was Slim's manager, and they started, after the program they liked what we did, Slim and I really got together, played a few tunes. And everybody in the station was really jumping, you know, and it turned out that Martin Block asked me, and Slim asked me would I team up with Slim to make -- see what we can do.
Start an act, which did happen. Slim asked me to join permanently, see, which I did. Now, we

have to find a name for myself, you know, which we got together and started on and what would match Slim, you know. And, of course, we took a long time to think about it, and it didn't come easy because Slim -- Slim's name was all right, but Slim and Leroy didn't sound so good, you know.

And we thought and we thought, Slim and Slap or something. We were trying to think of a name that was, would be close to the bass fiddle. So it turned up that slamming around at the bass kind of came to us. Maybe if we used the name Slam, Slim and Slam came to us. So that's how it came about, the Slim and the Slam.
Right. About what year was this?
Almost right -- almost, very soon after you arrived in New York?
